_help: Single-stack environment profile. It has TWO roles, same schema: (1) a SHAREABLE CATALOG profile — reusable across projects, lives OUTSIDE the plugin (a dir like ~/.kuru/profiles/, or your private GitLab), one file per build flavor (a gradle profile, a pnpm profile, …), an INPUT; and (2) a RESOLVED profile — this project's per-target environment of record, committed under .kuru/profiles/, the OUTPUT. /kuru:charter is the bridge: it matches a catalog profile to each app (or, if none matches, GENERATES one from the charter Q&A), lets you tweak it, and writes the resolved profile that the target's `profile` pointer in config.json refers to. `kuru env <id>` then reads slice -> target -> resolved profile so the builder/verifier know the real topology before choosing how to build/verify. Point init at a catalog: `kuru init --profile <DIR|URL>` takes a single location — a local directory of *.json, a single .json file, or an http(s) URL to a hosted catalog (GitHub contents / GitLab repository-tree API; the engine reads GITHUB_TOKEN/GITLAB_TOKEN for private repos). The catalog profile is GUIDANCE, not gospel: 'stack' seeds the initial gate preset at init; 'config', 'environment', and 'conventions' are read+confirmed by /kuru:charter. Internal URLs are fine here; gitignore the catalog copy if you prefer (the resolved .kuru/profiles/ copy is meant to be committed).

config._help: OPTIONAL. Omit to just use the 'stack' preset. If present, /kuru:charter uses these gate commands as the STARTING POINT for this flavor's gates (it confirms/tailors them with you first — they are not applied verbatim). In a multi-app repo this becomes this profile's TARGET gates. Air-gapped example: gradle --offline against a populated cache.

environment.verification_access: Dependencies (mongo, kafka) run IN-CLUSTER and are NOT reachable from outside the cluster. A verifier must obtain evidence by exec'ing into the deployed app pod (kubectl exec) or via in-cluster jobs — NOT by standing up an external integration test that dials mongo/kafka directly (it cannot reach them and will always fail). State here, per env, how to reach the running system + its deps and what NOT to assume; `kuru env <id>` surfaces this to the builder/verifier, and the contract critic uses it to judge whether an acceptance criterion is verifiable here.

airgap.notes: no internet during build; init.gradle points at the mirror; gradle runs --offline

conventions._help: OPTIONAL. Reusable 'how we build here' rules that are NOT gate commands — the org-specific tooling/skills a builder must use. /kuru:charter folds these into the charter's 'Required tooling / conventions' section (confirming with you, asking only for gaps). Each 'verify' line is then enforced by the strongest mechanism that fits it: deterministic ones (a file exists, a string is/isn't present, a command exits 0) get COMPILED INTO A `setup-conformance` GATE in config.json — machine-checked on every slice that uses that gate set (per target, in a multi-app repo); judgmental ones become acceptance criteria the verifier checks, with the 'rule' named in slice context as the cheapest path. IMPORTANT: state every 'verify' as a CHECKABLE FACT about the resulting artifact — the harness can only enforce OUTCOMES, never 'did the agent invoke skill X'. A rule with no checkable 'verify' cannot be enforced and will be treated as a soft suggestion.

build_setup.rule: Generate all Gradle build files via the `setup-gradle` skill — it encodes the air-gap mirror, version catalog, and plugin set. Do NOT hand-write them; hand-rolled versions get the mirror/plugins wrong and fail the offline build gate.
verify: settings.gradle.kts / init.gradle point repositories at the internal nexus mirror, not Maven Central
gradle/libs.versions.toml exists and pins plugin and library versions via the catalog
